newsitem.title: UK: ASDA rejects Alka Seltzer price rise.
newsitem.headline: ASDA rejects Alka Seltzer price rise.

text.p: British supermarket group ASDA Plc skirmished again over fixed prices on healthcare products on Thursday as it refused to implement a price rise on Warner Lambert's stomach upset treatment Alka Seltzer.
ASDA said it would not implement the price rise "unless forced to do so", and would consider taking the product off its shelves if legal action were taken.

The supermarket group has battled against the Retail Price Maintenance (RPM) on healthcare products since first challenging it nearly a year ago. Earlier this year it stopped stocking Anadin Paracetamol after an attempt to cut its in-store price.
In today's action, ASDA said it would not stock small packs of Alka Seltzer which have had the contents reduced, saying the cut from 12 tablets to 10 was equal to a 20 percent price rise.

"This double price attack on consumers is enough to give anyone an upset stomach," ASDA chief executive Allan Leighton said in a statement. "Taking out two tablets is a crude attempt to hide a 20 percent price rise," he added.

The Office of Fair Trading is expected to report next week on an inquiry into RPM on healthcare, which producers claim protects small neighbourhood pharmacies which would otherwise have to close in face of supermarket competition.
